subject: History
course: Grade 9 - World History and Geography to 1500 A.D

standards.description: Apply history and social science skills to analyze and communicate historical information.

skills.description: Select and synthesize evidence from artifacts, primary and secondary sources, charts, graphs, and diagrams related to world history.
Apply geographic skills to determine and predict patterns and trends of people, places, and events.
Construct arguments using evidence from multiple sources.
Investigate and analyze evidence from multiple sources to construct arguments and draw conclusions.
Compare and contrast historical, cultural, economic, and political perspectives.
Determine cause and effect to analyze connections between historical events.
Use economic decision-making models to analyze incentives and consequences of choices.
Engage and communicate as a civil and informed individual with different perspectives.
Develop products that reflect understanding of research and content.
Contextualize and corroborate sources to evaluate credibility, propaganda, and bias.

domains.name: Paleolithic Era into the Agricultural Revolution Neolithic Era

standards.description: Describe the period from the Paleolithic era into the Neolithic era using archaeological and geographic evidence.

skills.description: Describe archaeological evidence of the first humans and their geographic locations.
Explain the effect of geography on the emergence and migration of hunter-gatherer societies.
Describe characteristics of hunter-gatherer societies, including their use of tools and fire.
Analyze how technological and social developments led to sedentary settlements.
Analyze how archaeological discoveries change current understanding of early societies.

domains.name: Social, Cultural, Political, and Economic Development of Early Societies

standards.description: Describe early societies in the Fertile Crescent, including Egypt, Nubia, Mesopotamia, Israelites, and Phoenicians.

skills.description: Locate and explain the development of Egypt and Nubia.
Locate and explain the development of Mesopotamia.
Describe the development of the Israelites and the origins, beliefs, traditions, customs, persecution, and spread of Judaism.
Describe the development of the Phoenicians.

standards.description: Describe ancient Asian societies, including India, China, and their cultural and religious developments.

skills.description: Analyze the impact of geography on the development of ancient India and China, including locating them in time and place and describing their major geographic features.
Describe the social, cultural, political, and economic characteristics of the Indian subcontinent, including contributions and the concepts of varna and Jati.
Describe the origins, beliefs, customs, and spread of Hinduism.
Describe the origins, beliefs, customs, and spread of Buddhism.
Describe the social, cultural, political, and economic development of ancient China.
Describe the influence of Confucianism, Taoism, and Legalism.

standards.description: Understand Persia and Greece, including their geography, political systems, and cultural contributions.

skills.description: Describe the major geographic features of the region and analyze the effect of geography on its development.
Describe the social, cultural, political, and economic aspects of ancient Persia.
Describe the social, cultural, political, and economic development of Greece, including the significance of Athens and Sparta, the development of citizenship, and the different forms of democracy.
Evaluate the causes and consequences of the Persian and Peloponnesian wars.
Evaluate the significance of Alexander the Great's conquest of Greece and the formation and spread of Hellenistic culture.
Explain the influence of ancient Greek contributions, including science, art, architecture, philosophy, and mathematics, on the present day.

standards.description: Understand Rome and the Byzantine Empire, including their political structures, cultural developments, and religious transformations.

skills.description: Describe the influence of geography on Rome's development and the factors that threatened territorial cohesion.
Compare and contrast the political, social, and religious structure and development of the Roman Republic and the Roman Empire.
Describe the social, cultural, political, and economic development of the Byzantine Empire, including the establishment of Constantinople and the eventual division of the Roman Empire.

Describe the origins, beliefs, customs, and spread of Christianity, including the persecution of Christians throughout the Roman Empire and the eventual adoption and transmission of Christianity and the New Testament.
Describe differences between the Eastern and Western churches and the influence of Christianity throughout Europe, Middle Asia, the Middle East, and North Africa.
Explain the influence of Rome, including citizenship, slavery, Roman law and guaranteed rights, Roman art, architecture, engineering, and philosophy.

standards.description: Understand Islamic societies, including their origins, expansions, and cultural and economic contributions.

skills.description: Identify the physical features and describe the relationship between climate, land, and surrounding bodies of water, as well as nomadic and sedentary ways of life of the Arabian Peninsula.
Describe the origins, beliefs, traditions, customs, persecution, and spread of Islam.
Explain the significance of the Qur'an and the Sunnah as the primary sources of Islamic beliefs, practice, and law, and their influence in Muslims' daily lives.

Describe the expansion of territory under Muslim rule, the spread of Islam and the Arabic language among people in these territories, and the cultural and religious acceptance of Islam and the Arabic language.

Describe the growth of cities and the role of merchants in Muslim society and the expansion of trade routes in Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Indian Ocean, identifying the products and inventions that traveled along these routes.

standards.description: Understand the civilizations of China in the Middle Ages, including their political, cultural, and technological developments.

skills.description: Describe the reunification of China under the Tang Dynasty and reasons for the spread of Buddhism in Tang China, Korea, and Japan.
Describe agricultural, technological, and commercial developments during the Tang and Sung periods.
Analyze the influences of Confucianism and changes in Confucian thought during the Sung and Mongol periods.
Explain the importance of overland trade and maritime expeditions between China and other civilizations in the Mongol Ascendancy and Ming Dynasty.
Trace the historic influence of the tea trade, the manufacture of paper, the development of woodblock printing, the invention of the compass, and the invention of gunpowder.
Describe the development of the imperial state and the scholar-official class.

standards.description: Describe the sub-Saharan civilizations of Ghana and Mali in medieval Africa, including their economic and cultural developments.

skills.description: Describe the Niger River and the relationship of vegetation zones of forest, savannah, and desert to trade in gold, salt, food, and enslaved people, as well as the growth of the Ghana and Mali empires.
Analyze the importance of family, labor specialization, and regional commerce in the development of states and cities in West Africa.
Describe the role of the trans-Saharan caravan trade in the changing religious and cultural characteristics of West Africa and the influence of Islam.
Trace the growth of the Arabic language in government, trade, and Islam.
Describe the importance of written and oral traditions in the transmission of African history and culture.

standards.description: Understand the civilizations of medieval Japan, including their cultural, political, and social structures.

skills.description: Describe the significance of Japan's proximity to China and Korea and the intellectual, linguistic, religious, and philosophical influence of those countries on Japan.
Discuss the reign of Prince Shōtoku of Japan and the characteristics of Japanese society and family life during his reign.
Describe the values, social customs, and traditions prescribed by the lord-vassal system consisting of shogun, daimyo, and samurai and the lasting influence of the warrior code in the 21st century.
Trace the development of distinctive forms of Japanese Buddhism.
Examine the ninth and 10th centuries' golden age of literature, art, and drama and its lasting effects on culture today, including Murasaki Shikibu's Tale of Genji.
Analyze the rise of a military society in the late 12th century and the role of the samurai in that society.

standards.description: Understand the civilizations of medieval Europe, including their political, social, and economic structures.

skills.description: Describe the geography of the European and Eurasian landmass, including location, topography, waterways, vegetation, and climate, and their relationship to ways of life in medieval Europe.
Describe the spread of Christianity north of the Alps and the roles played by the early church and by monasteries in its diffusion after the fall of the western half of the Roman Empire.
Explain the development and role of feudalism in the medieval European economy and the role of the manor as the center of feudal relationships at the foundation of the political order.
Describe the growth of towns and trade as Europe emerged from feudalism.

standards.description: Analyze the conflict and cooperation between the papacy and European monarchs in medieval Europe.

skills.description: Explain the significance of developments in medieval English legal and constitutional practices, including the Magna Carta, parliaments, development of habeas corpus, and independent judiciary in England.
Analyze the reasons for the Great Schism in 1054.
Trace the causes and course of the Crusades and the effects on the Christian, Muslim, and Jewish populations in Europe and territorial claims.
Describe the decline of Muslim rule in the Iberian Peninsula that resulted in the expansion of Christian rule and the rise of Spanish and Portuguese kingdoms.
Explain the importance of the Catholic church as a political and intellectual institution and its effects on education, religious orders, preservation of languages and texts, and philosophy.

standards.description: Understand the Mesoamerican and Andean civilizations, including their political, cultural, and technological achievements.

skills.description: Describe the locations, landforms, and climates of Mexico, Central America, and South America and their effects on Mayan, Aztec, and Incan economies, trade, and the development of urban societies.
Explain how and where each empire arose and how the Aztec and Incan empires were defeated by the Spanish.
Describe the artistic and oral traditions and architecture in the three civilizations.
Describe the Mesoamerican achievements in astronomy and mathematics, including the development of the calendar and the effects of Mesoamerican knowledge of seasonal changes on agricultural systems.
Examine the roles of people in each society, including class structures, family life, warfare, religious beliefs and practices, and slavery.

standards.description: Understand the factors contributing to the European Renaissance, including its economic, political, and cultural foundations.

skills.description: Determine the economic, political, philosophical, and cultural foundations of the Italian Renaissance.
Sequence events related to the rise of Italian city-states and their political development, including Machiavelli's theory of governing.
Analyze the contributions of artists and philosophers of the Italian Renaissance, including Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Petrarch.
